parameters.content:
## Send a PDF receipt automatically after each Stripe payment

### Who's it for

Anyone selling through Stripe who wants customers to get a branded, itemised receipt as a PDF attachment — not just Stripe's default email. Works for one-off charges and for subscription renewals, since both produce a `charge.succeeded` event.

### How it works

The Stripe Trigger fires on every successful charge. A Code node turns the charge into receipt fields: money formatted in the charge's own currency (zero-decimal currencies handled), the card brand and last four digits, the customer's name and email. The HTML template is posted to an HTTP endpoint that returns a signed link, and a second request downloads it as a file so Gmail and Drive receive the same binary.

Charges without a customer email are stopped by the If node instead of failing in Gmail.

### How to set up

1. Connect your Stripe account to the **Stripe Trigger** node. n8n registers the webhook for you.
2. Put your company name, address, support email and locale in **Set company details**.
3. Add a Header Auth credential named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer YOUR_KEY`. Get the key at [emitforge.com/start](https://emitforge.com/start?from=n8n) — the free tier covers 100 receipts a month and needs no card.
4. Connect Gmail, and optionally Google Drive and Slack (delete those two nodes if you don't need them).
5. Make a test payment in Stripe test mode and check the receipt lands in your inbox.

### Requirements

Stripe and Gmail credentials (Google Drive and Slack optional), plus an API key for the rendering endpoint — free tier at [emitforge.com/start](https://emitforge.com/start?from=n8n), 100 renders a month, no card.

### How to customize

To itemise a receipt, put `metadata.items` on the charge as `desc|qty|unit;desc|qty|unit` — the Code node turns it into table rows. To use `payment_intent.succeeded` instead, change the event in the trigger and read `data.object` the same way. To use your own typeface, embed it as a data URI; the renderer has one font installed and any other family falls back silently.

## Step 1: Catch the payment

Stripe calls this workflow the moment a charge succeeds. Company details live in one Set node so they are edited in a single place.

## Step 2: Build the receipt and render it

The Code node reads the real charge fields (amount, currency, receipt_email, description, card) and formats them. Charges with no email are stopped here. The HTTP request posts the HTML and gets back a signed link; the second request downloads it as a file.

No key yet? Sign up at [emitforge.com/start](https://emitforge.com/start?from=n8n) and it arrives by email.

## Step 3: Deliver

Gmail sends the receipt as an attachment and Drive archives the same file in parallel. Slack gets a one-line summary so you can see the run without opening anything.
